summary: Port reproduces the original's 6-px segmented rainbow 'leg' train exactly in spatial structure, palette walk and mean crawl speed, but replaces the original's smooth sinusoidal speed undulation (5.4-14.2 px/s, 2.6x swing) with a two-level square-wave toggle (7.8 / 10.7 px/s, 1.4x swing), so the port glides where the original visibly surges and stalls.
observations: Rig: 60-px strip, no controls on EITHER side (meta.json sides.orig.controls and sides.port.controls are both empty; --probe-controls prints '(no settable controls)' for both). wantsSensors false on both.
Both sides compile and run clean over 300 s of simulated time (no compileError/runtimeError in any run, including --skip 300).

STRUCTURE — identical. Both sides satisfy pixel[i+1] == pixel[i+6] for 83% of indices at every dumped time (best L=6 for both, identical hit-rates 6:0.83 / 11:0.65 / 16:0.48). i.e. both draw 6-pixel 'segments' whose colour ramp advances one step per segment — the millipede-leg look.

SPATIAL SPECTRUM — identical to within 0.1 unit. Mean |X(k)| over 201 dumped frames, orig vs port: k=1 20.6/20.5, k=3 1.5/1.5, k=9 7.5/7.5, k=11 20.6/20.5, k=12 8.9/8.9, k=13 4.2/4.2, k=19 5.5/5.5, k=21 7.5/7.5, k=24 4.3/4.3. Every harmonic matches; there is no missing or extra spatial component.

BRIGHTNESS / DUTY — identical. 60 s survey meanBrightness avg 47.5 on both, min 46 max 49 on both, brightnessTrend 'steady' on both, zeroMotionFrames 1 on both. Over the 201-frame dump: dark fraction (max channel < 16) 0.346 orig vs 0.333 port; 8-bin max-channel histogram matches within 1.5 pp in every bin; dark-run-length histogram 1:433/2:424/3:609/4:267 (orig) vs 1:452/2:434/3:650/4:186 (port).

COLOUR — identical and phase-locked, even at t=300 s. 60 s survey: meanR avg 47.9 both, meanG 47.8 both, meanB 46.9/46.9. Palette-walk period from autocorrelation of meanR/G/B is 33 frames @5fps = 6.60 s on BOTH sides, with matching peak heights out to lag 98 (0.89 both) in a 180 s survey. In the --skip 300 window meanR avg 50.8/50.8, meanG 46.7/46.7, meanB 45.1/45.1, first/last within 1 unit on every channel. No hue drift accumulates.

MEAN SPEED — identical. Sub-pixel circular cross-correlation of consecutive dumped frames gives a mean translation of -9.0 px/s on both sides (orig -8.84/-8.96/-8.98, port -9.00/-9.01/-9.05 at 10/20/40 fps). Motion is leftward (toward pixel 0) on both.

FPS-INVARIANCE — both sides are time-based, not frame-stepped: mean velocity -9.0 px/s at 10, 20 and 40 fps on both, and the modulation waveform is unchanged across the three rates. No frame-rate coupling on either side.

THE DIVERGENCE — speed-modulation WAVEFORM. Instantaneous velocity (cross-correlation, 0.1 s steps, confirmed independently by k=11 DFT-phase tracking and reproduced at 10/20/40 fps): ORIGINAL sweeps smoothly and continuously, e.g. -14.2 -13.6 -13.4 -12.8 -12.0 -10.2 -10.0 -8.8 -7.8 -7.0 -6.4 -5.8 -5.4 -5.4 -5.6 -5.4 -5.6 -6.0 -6.4 -7.0 -8.2 -8.6 -9.6 -10.4 -11.2 -12.4 -12.6 -13.4 -13.8 -13.8 -14.2 px/s — a sinusoid between about -5.4 and -14.2 px/s (2.6x swing, +/-49% of mean). PORT sits on two flat plateaus with ~0.2 s transitions: -10.8 -10.8 -10.6 x14 ... -8.4 -8.2 -8.0 -8.0 -7.8 -7.8 -8.0 -7.6 x13 ... -8.4 -10.0 -10.6 -10.8 — i.e. it toggles between -10.7 and -7.9 px/s (1.37x swing, +/-16% of mean).

The modulation PERIOD matches: ~3.2 s on the original (velocity autocorrelation peak 0.61 at lag 3.2 s), ~3.1-3.3 s on the port (high plateau ~1.6 s, low plateau ~1.4 s). That is exactly half the 6.60 s palette cycle on both sides, so the port has the right rhythm and the wrong shape.

The same divergence shows up for free in the motion stat: over --skip 300 --seconds 12 --fps 20, orig motion {avg 22.6, min 1, max 43} vs port {avg 21.1, min 9, max 33} — equal averages, but the original's motion dips ~9x lower and peaks ~30% higher because it genuinely stalls and surges. Same signature at seed 7 and seed 1234 (orig min 0 max 43, port min 0 max 34).

VISUALLY (240-px waterfall, tools/verify/out/millipede/big240 and late/): the original's rainbow bands are pronounced S-curves — long near-vertical (near-stationary) stretches alternating with steep dives — which reads as a crawling, undulating millipede gait. The port's bands are near-uniform diagonals with a single mild kink per 3.2 s cycle; it reads as a steady drift with a slight hesitation.
DETERMINISM — neither side uses RNG: seeds 1, 7 and 1234 give byte-equal summary stats on both sides, so the comparison is not seed-dependent.

Same-time, same-index pixel agreement is poor (mean abs channel diff ~67 unshifted, ~11 at the best pure spatial shift) but that is phase, not structure: per-frame search over (time offset, spatial shift) finds port frames matching original frames to a mean abs diff of 0.9-4.4 (out of a mean level of 48) at many times. The two sides are drawing the same picture at a wandering relative phase, which is the direct consequence of the different speed-modulation waveform.
feedback: Everything except one axis is already right: segment length (6 px), the per-segment colour-ramp advance, the full spatial harmonic content, mean brightness (47.5), dark duty (~34%), the 6.60 s palette cycle and its phase (still locked at t=300 s), the mean crawl speed (-9.0 px/s leftward), and time-based (fps-invariant) stepping. Do not touch any of those.

The single fix needed: the port's crawl speed is a TWO-STATE SQUARE WAVE and the original's is a SMOOTH CONTINUOUS SWEEP. Port toggles between 7.9 and 10.7 px/s with ~1.5 s dwells and ~0.2 s transitions; the original glides continuously through every speed from 5.4 px/s to 14.2 px/s and back. Whatever term modulates the leg advance needs to vary continuously (sinusoidally) rather than snapping between discrete levels — the plateau shape suggests the port is quantizing or thresholding a value that should be used raw.

The modulation DEPTH is also too shallow by ~3x. Original: +/-4.4 px/s around a -9.2 px/s mean (peak/trough ratio 2.6). Port: +/-1.4 px/s around a -9.2 px/s mean (ratio 1.37). After making the modulation continuous, its amplitude should reach roughly 0.5x the mean speed in each direction so the pattern nearly stalls at the slow phase.
The modulation PERIOD is already correct (~3.2 s, i.e. half the 6.60 s palette cycle) — keep it; only the waveform and amplitude need changing.

Quick regression check for a fixer: measure sub-pixel per-frame translation (cross-correlate consecutive frames) over ~10 s and look at the velocity series. A correct port produces a smooth sinusoid spanning about -5 to -14 px/s; the current port produces a square wave spanning -8 to -11. Equivalently, `motion` min over a 12 s window at 20 fps should fall to ~1 (it is currently 9) while max rises to ~43 (currently 33), with the average staying near 22.
No control-surface work needed: both sides genuinely expose zero controls.
